messages:
maria: FYI getting a bunch of 'prometheus_remote_storage_queue_length' alerts for cluster-eu-west-1, looks correlated with scrape failures. dashboard shows queue length spiking to ~120k for a few hours.
aj: seen it, alerts started ~10:12 UTC. Are these coming from sidecars or direct node_exporter jobs?
maria: mostly from sidecar -> remote_write pipelines. node-exporter scrapes look fine individually, but remote_write backpressure is high.
remotewrite-bot: ALERT: remotewrite_queue_length > 50k for 12m on cluster-eu-west-1 (affected sharded-remote-writes: rw-pool-A,B)
liam: logs show timeout errors to s3-compatible endpoint for one replica, but that doesn't explain the cardinality spike we got earlier. Any relabel changes rolled recently?
natalie: we rolled a relabel_config for `k8s_pod_name` -> `pod_name` normalization yesterday afternoon to try reduce label mismatches. Might have introduced a regex that didn't drop container_id.
maria: copying the relabel snippet we applied:
```yaml
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app, __meta_kubernetes_pod_name]
  regex: (.+);(.+)\-([0-9a-f]{12})
  target_label: pod_name
  replacement: $1
  action: replace
- source_labels: [container_id]
  regex: (.+)
  action: keep
```
maria: note the `action: keep` on container_id — that was intended for debugging but left in prod.
aj: oh that would keep container_id as a label -> massive cardinality. That explains the spike. Can we drop it quickly?
liam: +1. propose a quick patch to change `action: keep` -> `action: drop` and then restart the scrape config roll.
natalie: I'm on it. Pushing change to prometheus-config map now. Rolling patch to prometheus-eu-west-1-0 (shard A) first.
sam: ran `kubectl exec -n monitoring prometheus-eu-west-1-0 -- curl -s localhost:9090/-/reload` after configmap update.
liam: good. Also increase remote_write timeout from 30s -> 60s temporarily to avoid immediate backpressure while relabel settles. Edit in the remote_write stanza.
maria: made the timeout bump on shard A; applying to shard B now.
aj: observed queue length drop from 120k -> 30k on shard A within 8m. shard B still high, patching in progress.
remotewrite-bot: INFO: remote_write queue drain rate improved on shard-A (estimated catch-up time 13m)
liam: follow-up - we should add a unit test to our config CI to detect `action: keep` on container_id or any label matching `container*`/`id`. That would prevent accidental high-card labels.
natalie: opened GH PR #3124 with a lint rule and a small test harness.
aj: question—did the relabel change also affect any Prometheus federations? I see a slight uptick in duplicated label warnings in the federation logs.
maria: federation scrapes flagged `label_format` warnings for some metrics. I reverted the federation scrape to read-only mode for the affected targets. Can ops team monitor for duplicate series alerts?
liam: will add a Grafana panel to show series_count_by_job for the top 20 jobs so we can quickly catch repeats.
aj: re: alert tuning — we should silence the remote_write queue alert for 15m on eu-west while rolling patches. Otherwise it noisy-pagers the oncall.
maria: silenced on-call, thanks.
atalie: after the drop, cardinality looks back to normal; series_count normalized and disk usage for TSDB stable. Rolling the config to remaining shards now.
sam: note for postmortem — root cause: debug relabel step left `action: keep` on a high-cardinality label (container_id). Contributing factors: no CI lint, short remote_write timeout exacerbated backlog.
liam: agreed. Action items: 1) CI relabel lint (Natalie) 2) Add series_count_by_job Grafana (Liam) 3) Increase default remote_write timeout to 60s for clusters behind flaky egress (Maria) 4) Postmortem doc (Sam)
maria: I'll draft postmortem and include exact timestamps, impacted shards, and cost estimate for extra ingestion during spike. Estimated additional ingested series ~1.2M over 3h.
aj: thanks everyone. keep monitoring for any residual queue growth.
liam: closing thread once shard-B shows <5k queue and no duplicate-label alerts for 30m. ping here when done.
remotewrite-bot: RESOLVED: remotewrite_queue_length on shard-A cleared. shard-B still clearing (50% drained).
